scope: Acknowledgments for documented advice, prior research, reference tools, direct project work and AI collaboration.
note: Credit does not imply endorsement, authorship of Project Epoch, permission to reuse assets, or that every historical annotation is correct. Original licenses and detailed source provenance remain controlling. Study and review credits are separate from installed art and runtime testing.

entries.name: Justin (justin3009)
entries.contribution: Earlier Project Schala and eighth-character experiments, and practical explanations of follower ordering, Gaspar and palette pressure, portraits, stats, RAM and SRAM pitfalls. His experience helped shape Project Epoch's regression checklist.
entries.limit: Acknowledgment of earlier work and advice; no claim that Justin supplied or authored the installed Epoch portrait or world-map art.

entries.name: Mauron, Vehek and JLukas
entries.contribution: Character-record, graphics, animation, menu, Tech and naming maps, historical eighth-character experiments, and PC-before-NPC ordering guidance. Their published work supplied concrete addresses, hypotheses and failure cases that this project checked.
links: Historical mapping audit and original post citations
entries.limit: Existing discoveries are credited even where later checks correct an annotation. Historical component patches are not imported into the current build.

entries.name: FaustWolf
entries.contribution: Published Magus graphics, palette, assembly and animation boundary notes used in the historical Schala comparison, with Vehek's later assembly-size correction retained.

entries.name: OnemusCT, Pseudoarc and Temporal Redux / Jets of Time contributors
entries.contribution: Event parsing, PC/name lookups, object-copy insertion and object-call adjustment implementation references; Pseudoarc's ctrando also informed the later Tech-package research.

entries.name: dscotton and DocDamage
entries.contribution: Public Chrono Trigger disassembly and annotation references used to locate and cross-check native code paths. Project Epoch records corrections rather than assuming every label or interpretation is authoritative.

entries.name: Chrono Compendium, Kajar Laboratories and Data Crystal contributors
entries.contribution: Preservation of forum discussions, historical experiments, graphics and portrait tutorials, event-language documentation, and RAM/Tech mapping. These archives made earlier work discoverable and checkable.
links: Data Crystal Chrono Trigger RAM map

entries.name: Oswego del Fuego and the historical Schala art contributors
entries.contribution: Historical Schala art studies reviewed as reference. The preserved composite associated with justin3009 credits portions to Oswego del Fuego; it is not attributed wholly to Justin.
entries.evidence_note: Attribution inspected on the preserved composite's footer during the October 20 art reinspection; the source image remains local.
entries.limit: The historical composite was not imported into the installed world-map, main-pose or portrait assets.

entries.name: Sour and the Mesen contributors
entries.contribution: Mesen's emulator, debugger, scripting and source enabled native traces, controller-driven checks, screenshots and state inspection. Its BPS implementation also supplied the independent patch-format check.

entries.name: Asar authors and contributors
entries.contribution: 65C816 assembly tooling used for independent assembly and byte-equality checks of authored helpers.

entries.name: byuu / Near and BPS specification preservers
entries.contribution: The public-domain BPS format specification used by the original deterministic patch codec; the Flips repository preserves the referenced specification.
entries.limit: Specification credit; Flips is not claimed as the executed verification tool.

entries.name: bsnes, Snes9x, Libretro and RetroArch contributors
entries.contribution: Emulation cores, replay infrastructure and source references used in the earlier diagnostic and timing work.

entries.name: Ghidra contributors and joshleaves / ghidra-snes
entries.contribution: Disassembly tooling and SNES language/loader support tested during the recompilation comparison.
entries.limit: Research tooling, not a replacement for native validation or the basis of a released PC port.

entries.name: ThisIsAkill / ct-recomp and RetroPortingToolKit / snesrecomp contributors
entries.contribution: Comparative recompilation research: ct-recomp was built and tested; snesrecomp was inspected and used to generate synthetic output, without compiling or executing that generated C++. These experiments informed the decision to keep native SNES work primary.
entries.limit: Research comparison credit; no claim of copied project code or a Project Epoch PC release.

entries.name: Andrei Pemberton
entries.contribution: Project direction, preservation and design requirements, in-game review, visual selection and supplied screenshots.

entries.name: Coda / OpenAI Codex
entries.contribution: Implementation, source research, runtime tracing, evidence reconciliation, selected V5 world-map sprites, targeted art integration, front/rear casting refinements and publication.

entries.name: OpenAI image-generation tool
entries.contribution: Concept-derived Schala portrait candidates, refined through reference-guided iterations and converted into a separate SNES palette/tile asset by Coda.
entries.limit: The installed portrait is generated, concept-derived art; it is not a literal Toriyama drawing or a wholly hand-drawn portrait.

entries.name: Lily (Lilitari) / ChatGPT
entries.contribution: Selected horizontal casting preparation/release poses; independent world-map and main-character art studies; visual/source review and development-update review.
entries.limit: Review of supplied material is not independent emulator execution.

entries.name: Red / Claude Cowork
entries.contribution: Selected recoil and KO art; the earlier world-map engineering pilot and independent main-character sprite studies.

entries.name: Wren / Grok Bot
entries.contribution: Independent world-map and main-character sprite studies used in the art comparison.
entries.limit: Study credit; these complete sprite sets were not selected for installation.

entries.name: Gemini
entries.contribution: Independent world-map and main-character pixel-art proposals, including returned code/JSON reconstructed locally for comparison.
entries.limit: Study credit; local reconstruction does not imply provider-side execution or installed art.

entries.name: Nua / Muse
entries.contribution: Independent world-map and main-character pixel-grid studies, reconstructed from returned JSON and compared with the retail references.
entries.limit: Study credit; these sets were not selected for installation.

entries.name: Meta AI
entries.contribution: Independent world-map and main-character sprite studies and returned image/source material used in the comparison.
entries.limit: Study credit; these sets were not selected for installation.

entries.name: Claude Code
entries.contribution: Separate source and visual critique, including the unresolved projectile-alignment evidence and prismatic color-study tradeoffs.
entries.limit: The recorded image/source critique did not inspect the ROM bytes or run the emulator.

entries.name: Additional Codex/ChatGPT reviewers and the separate Grok review route
entries.contribution: Bounded code, interrupt/timing and evidence critiques documented in the individual review receipts. This Grok route is distinct from Wren's personal Grok Bot conversation.
entries.limit: Only returned reviews count as contributions; failed or unavailable routes are not credited as completed review.

entries.name: Project Epoch branding — Coda, Lily and OpenAI image generation
entries.contribution: Coda: composition, generation briefs, iteration and integration. Lily: art direction and visual review, including the smaller cameo and clearer title hierarchy. OpenAI image-generation tool: rendered artwork. Andrei: direction and approved portrait likeness.
entries.limit: Generated branding illustrations; no native game change or new gameplay evidence.

entries.name: Square's Chrono Trigger team and Akira Toriyama
entries.contribution: The original game, retail sprites and character designs supply the visual and mechanical reference for this fan research. Schala's concept design informed the portrait and sprite refinements.
entries.limit: Chrono Trigger and its original artwork belong to their respective rights holders.
